description: Provisional relationship labels for the Climate Change & Education evidence base, aligned with Venegas Marin, Schwarz, and Sabarwal (2024) Figure 1. Evidence Mapping distinguishes review synthesis from original causal estimation; Effect Summary rows require primary-study review.

relationships.label: Weather Shock → Learning
relationships.summary: Effect of extreme weather (heat, storms, drought, wildfire/air quality) on short-run learning measures such as test scores or learning progress.

relationships.label: Weather Shock → Schooling
relationships.summary: Effect on enrollment, dropout, attendance, grade progression, or longer-term educational attainment.

relationships.label: Weather Shock → School Disruption
relationships.summary: Effect on school access, closures, damaged infrastructure, or school environmental conditions that interrupt instruction.

relationships.label: Weather Shock → Household Vulnerability
relationships.summary: Household economic shocks, coping responses, or poverty channels that alter schooling demand or investment.

relationships.label: Weather Shock → Health & Nutrition
relationships.summary: Health or nutritional mechanisms linking weather extremes to student readiness or capacity to learn.

relationships.label: School Disruption → Learning
relationships.summary: Link from disrupted instruction (e.g., closure days) to learning loss. Distinguish total weather effects from empirically identified mediation in primary studies.

relationships.label: Adaptation → Educational Outcomes
relationships.summary: Causal or quasi-experimental evidence on adaptation/resilience interventions (infrastructure, scheduling, safety nets) improving educational outcomes. Conceptual policy discussion alone does not satisfy this relationship.
